answer: In a decentralized network, a Sybil-resistant mechanism utilizes a reputation system anchored to a physical proof-of-work, such as a quartz timestamped cryptographic puzzle. Each agent must broadcast a solution to the puzzle, effectively whispering its authenticity to the network. This creates a secure haven against Sybil attacks, as generating multiple identities becomes computationally expensive, costing an attacker a minimum of 51% of the network's computational power, thereby making it economically infeasible.
